# Introduction

In this lab, you will use `rvest` functions to scrape data from the internet, and employ data visualization best practices to communicate insights. Several of the web-scraping steps will be done together in class.

## Learning goals

By the end of this lab, you should be able to:

+ Use `rvest` functions to read html tables from the internet 
+ Write and read data files
+ Create presentation-ready visualizations 

## Load packages

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

# Exercises

::: callout-note
### Exercise 1: Social Security Example

Note, we scraped this data together in class. You can re-use your scraping code, but the visualization should explore something different or additional to what was created in class.

+ In an R script, write code to scrape this table of Social Security data from [this website](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/babynames/numberUSbirths.html)
+ Use code to save the file (.csv, .rds, or .xlsx)
+ In a .qmd, read in the saved data file
+ Produce a presentation-ready visualization that illustrates a key insight from the data.

:::

::: callout-note
### Exercise 2: State populations

Repeat the steps in Exercise 1 for the state population data on [this webpage](https://simple.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_by_population). 

:::

::: callout-note

### Exercise 3

Repeat the steps in Exercise 1 for the Pennsylvania System of School Assessment data on [this webpage](https://www.education.pa.gov/DataAndReporting/Assessments/Pages/PSSA-Results.aspx). 

:::

::: callout-note
### Exercise 4

Repeat the steps in Exercise 1 for the Villanova Reddit data. 

:::

::: callout-note
### Exercise 5

Scrape the [100m Olympic record progression tables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_metres_at_the_Olympics) and create the following plot  


```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("./img/olympics.png")
```

:::

::: callout-note
### Exercise 6

+ Choose one additional website to scrape data from and provide a presentation-ready visualization that demonstrates insight gleaned from the data. 
+ You are encouraged to choose a topic you are personally interested in. Wikipedia pages often have tables to scrape, or Googling "top 25/50/100 _______" will often return websites that have rankings displayed in tables. 
+ For example, top 50 movies, YouTube channels, podcasts, books, happiest countries, causes of death, high-satisfaction jobs, highest-scoring athletes, etc etc.

:::
